s: Which of the following pairs of Acts constituted the three-capitals legislative framework of Andhra Pradesh in 2020?
o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020
AP Regional Balance Act, 2020 and Kurnool Judicial Capital Act, 2020
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and Six-Point Formula Act, 1973
AP Capital Development Act, 2019 and Amaravati Protection Act, 2021
x: The framework consisted of the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020.

s: Under the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020, which city was proposed as the executive capital?
x: The 2020 Act proposed Visakhapatnam as executive, Amaravati as legislative and Kurnool as judicial capital.

s: Kalyana Karnataka has special status under which Article of the Constitution?
x: Kalyana Karnataka has special status under Article 371J since 2013, although disparities continue.

s: Under the 2020 three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, which city was to be the judicial capital?
x: Kurnool was the judicial capital; Visakhapatnam executive and Amaravati legislative.

s: Which of the following Acts were withdrawn by the Andhra Pradesh Assembly in November 2021?
o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and Andhra State Act, 1953
AP Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019 and APCRDA Act, 2014
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and APCRDA Act, 2014
x: In November 2021 a Repeal Bill withdrew both three-capitals Acts of 2020: the Decentralisation Act and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act.

s:
Consider the following statements about the three-capitals legislation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The APCRDA (Repeal) Act was passed in 2020.
2. The Repeal Bill withdrawing the three-capitals Acts was introduced in the AP Assembly in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The APCRDA (Repeal) Act came in 2020; the Repeal Bill withdrawing the three-capitals Acts was introduced in November 2021, not 2023.

s: Under the 2020 three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, which city was to be the legislative capital?
x: Amaravati was the legislative capital, Visakhapatnam the executive and Kurnool the judicial capital.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bhargava Committee — Legal safeguards for Mulki employment
Wanchoo Committee — Assessment of Telangana surplus funds
Srikrishna Committee — Consultation on the Telangana/united Andhra Pradesh question
Sivaramakrishnan Committee — Investigation of literacy disparities
x: The Srikrishna Committee, headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, was appointed in 2010 to consult on the Telangana or united Andhra Pradesh question. The Bhargava Committee dealt with surplus funds, the Wanchoo Committee with Mulki safeguards, and the Sivaramakrishnan Committee with locating the new capital.

s: Which committee was constituted under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 as an expert committee for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Sivaramakrishnan Committee, headed by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan, was the expert committee under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which 1969 committee examined the diversion of Telangana's surplus funds to other regions?
x: The Bhargava Committee (1969) dealt with Telangana surplus funds; the Wanchoo Committee (1969) dealt with Mulki safeguards.

s: The Srikrishna Committee on the Telangana question (December 2010) gave how many options?
x: The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee (2010) offered six options on the Telangana / united AP question.

s: What was the mandate of the Wanchoo Committee (1969)?
o: To assess Telangana surplus funds diverted to other regions
To suggest ways to keep the Mulki (employment) safeguards
To select the site of the new capital of Andhra Pradesh
To give options on the Telangana question
x: The Wanchoo Committee (1969) looked at ways to keep Mulki safeguards; the Bhargava Committee (1969) dealt with surplus funds.

s: What was the appointed day under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 took effect on the appointed day, 2 June 2014.

s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, for up to how many years was Hyderabad made the common capital?
x: Hyderabad was the common capital for up to ten years; Sections 46(2)-(3) give the backward-areas package.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Special Category Status (SCS) debate for Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: PM's promise of SCS – Lok Sabha
End of general-versus-special distinction – Thirteenth Finance Commission
Alternative offered instead of SCS – Special assistance measure
x: A special assistance measure was offered instead of SCS. The PM promised SCS in the Rajya Sabha in February 2014, and it was the Fourteenth Finance Commission that ended the distinction.

s: The backward-areas package of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 covers how many districts?
x: The package covers 7 backward districts: 4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Andhra.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Each backward district gets a grant of Rs 50 crore per year.
The backward districts are 4 in North Andhra and 3 in Rayalaseema.
x: The 7 backward districts are 4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Andhra, not the reverse.

s: Which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides tax incentives to the residual State?
x: Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act provides tax incentives; Section 46(2)-(3) gives the backward-areas package.

s: Which Finance Commission ended the distinction between general and special category States?
x: The 14th Finance Commission ended the general/special distinction, so AP was offered a 'special assistance measure' instead of SCS.

s: Which of the following was set up under the 8-Point Formula of 1969?
o: Expert committee for locating the new capital of AP
x: The 8-Point Formula set up a high-level committee under a judge and a special committee on Telangana surpluses; the capital-location committee came under the 2014 Act.

s: Which Amendment inserted Article 371D, providing the zonal system of local cadres in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 32nd Amendment, 1973, following the Six Point Formula, inserted Articles 371D and 371E.

s: On which date was the Six Point Formula for Andhra Pradesh announced?
x: The Six Point Formula came on 21 September 1973 and led to the 32nd Amendment inserting Article 371D.

s: The Jai Andhra movement of 1972 was a reaction to the Supreme Court's decision upholding which of the following?
x: The Jai Andhra movement (1972) reacted to the Supreme Court upholding the Mulki rules and sought a separate Andhra.

s:
Consider the following statements about separate-state movements in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Jai Andhra movement started in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
2. The 2009-14 phase of the Telangana movement led to Telangana State in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Jai Andhra began in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, and the 2009-14 Telangana phase produced Telangana State in 2014.

s: Which Articles were inserted in the Constitution by the 32nd Amendment, 1973, following the Six Point Formula?
x: The 32nd Amendment, 1973 inserted Article 371D (zonal system of local cadres) and Article 371E (central university in AP).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the pre-2022 regional grouping of Andhra Pradesh's 13 districts?
o: North Andhra comprised Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam.
Rayalaseema comprised Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore were part of North Andhra.
Kadapa is also known as YSR district.
x: Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore were placed in Coastal Andhra, not North Andhra; the other statements are correct.

s: Under the pre-2022 public-employment zonal grouping, which districts formed Zone II?
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
x: Zone II comprised East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone I was North Andhra, Zone III Guntur-Prakasam-Nellore and Zone IV Rayalaseema.

s: NITI Aayog monitors how many Aspirational Districts?
x: NITI Aayog monitors 112 Aspirational Districts.

s: In which district of Rayalaseema is a JSW steel plant located?
x: The JSW steel plant is in Kadapa; Royal Enfield has a facility in Tirupati.

s: Which district has the highest per capita income in Andhra Pradesh (2025-26 AE)?
x: Visakhapatnam tops per capita income, with Krishna next; Kurnool is the lowest.

s:
Consider the following statements about regional disparity in Andhra Pradesh:
1. No Rayalaseema district reaches the State average per capita income.
2. Kurnool has the lowest per capita income.
3. Anantapur receives more rainfall than Srikakulam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Anantapur gets about 544 mm against up to 1,250 mm in Srikakulam-Vizianagaram.

s: What was the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh as per Census 2011?
x: AP's literacy rate in 2011 was 67.35%.

s: Which city in Rayalaseema is linked with Royal Enfield under the Rayalaseema industrial hub plan (2026)?
x: Under the 2026 Rayalaseema industrial hub plan, Royal Enfield is at Tirupati and the JSW steel plant at Kadapa.

s: In which year was the Gentlemen's Agreement, which reused the Sri Bagh template for Telangana safeguards, concluded?
x: The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded in 1956, not 1969; the Sri Bagh Pact was of 1937.

s: Who drafted the Sri Bagh Pact of 1937?
x: The Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937), the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord, was drafted by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: Under the Sri Bagh Pact, what was Rayalaseema given the choice of?
o: The capital or the Governor's residence
The High Court or the University
The capital or the High Court
x: The Sri Bagh Pact let Rayalaseema choose either the capital or the High Court; Andhra State's capital went to Kurnool in 1953.

s: In which year was the Sri Bagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders signed?
x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 16 November 1937 was the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord.

s: Under the National Youth Policy 2014, the term ‘youth’ refers to persons in which age group?
x: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as persons aged 15–29 years. The National Youth Policy 2003 used the age group 13–35 years.

s: How many priority areas does the National Youth Policy 2014 have?
x: NYP 2014 has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas, including participation in politics and governance and sports.

s: Under the National Youth Policy 2003, which age group did 'youth' cover?
x: NYP 2003 defined youth as 13-35 years; NYP 2014 narrowed it to 15-29.

s: In which year was India's first National Youth Policy adopted?
x: The first NYP came in 1988; National Youth Day and the Department of Youth Affairs date from 1985.

s: National Youth Day, observed since 1985, marks the birth anniversary of whom?
x: National Youth Day has been observed since 1985 on the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

s: How many objectives does the National Youth Policy 2014 set out?
x: The National Youth Policy 2014 has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports was set up in 1985.
2. Youth Affairs and Sports became a separate Ministry in 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Department of Youth Affairs and Sports came in 1985, and it became a separate Ministry in 2000.

s: What is the motto of the National Service Scheme (NSS)?
x: The NSS motto is 'Not Me But You'; the scheme, started in 1969, rests on the idea of 'Education through Service'.

s: MY Bharat, launched on 31 October 2023, replaced which organisation?
x: MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023 and replaced NYKS under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

s: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana under Skill India was launched in:
x: PMKVY under Skill India was launched in 2015 and provides skill training for new entrants to the job market.

s: The neighbourhood Youth Parliament is part of which programme launched in December 2014?
x: The National Young Leaders Programme (Dec 2014) includes the Neighbourhood Youth Parliament and National Youth Advisory Council.

s: In which year was the National Service Scheme (NSS) started?
x: NSS began in 1969 with the motto 'Not Me But You'.

s: What does the PM-Vidyalaxmi scheme provide?
x: PM-Vidyalaxmi gives students collateral-free education loans.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Persuasive agitation — overthrow of the existing system
Revolutionary agitation — overthrow of the system
Revolutionary agitation — opposition to attendance rules
x: Revolutionary agitation seeks to overthrow the system. Examination postponement is persuasive, while opposition to attendance rules is resistance.

s: In the life cycle of a youth agitation, which stage comes first?
x: The sequence is discontent, initiation, formalisation, public support and official action.

s: With whom is the relative deprivation theory of youth unrest associated?
x: Relative deprivation theory is associated with Stouffer; personal maladjustment is another listed theory.

s: What does youth unrest refer to?
o: A temporary disagreement between students and teachers over examinations
Individual frustration of a young person over personal failure
Organised violence carried out only by youth wings of political parties
Collective frustration among young people when social norms appear ineffective or harmful
x: Youth unrest is collective frustration among young people when society's norms seem ineffective or harmful.

s: A student protest demanding the postponement of an examination is an example of which type of youth unrest?
x: Exam postponement is persuasive unrest; a protest against attendance rules is resistance.

s: According to the resource mobilisation theory of youth unrest, what matters more than grievances?
x: Resource mobilisation theory stresses tactics and leadership over grievances; relative deprivation is Stouffer's theory.

s: What did the Anti-Mandal movement of 1990 oppose?
x: The Anti-Mandal movement opposed 27% reservation for OBCs.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nav Nirman movement — Gujarat — corruption and prices
x: The Nav Nirman movement of Gujarat involved students protesting corruption and prices. The other pairs interchange the states or issues of different movements.

s: What followed the NEET paper leak protests, which began at Jantar Mantar and turned nationwide?
o: A Supreme Court ban on protests at Jantar Mantar
x: The protests began at Jantar Mantar, turned nationwide and were followed by a ministerial resignation (5 Aug 2026).

s: Which was the first student-led national movement in India?
x: Swadeshi (1905) was the first student-led national movement; Young Bengal was the first youth organisation.

s: Who founded the Young Bengal movement, India's first youth organisation?
x: Young Bengal was founded by Derozio.

s: With which accord did the AASU movement (1979-85) end?
x: The AASU movement against illegal migrants ended with the Assam Accord of 1985.

s: In which State did the Nav Nirman student agitation of 1974 take place?
x: Nav Nirman was a Gujarat student agitation that forced CM Chimanbhai Patel to resign; JP led the separate Bihar movement.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Founder of the first youth reform movement – Henry Louis Vivian Derozio
First youth organisation of India – Young Bengal Movement
First student-led national movement – JP Movement, 1974
Leader of the 1974 Bihar student movement – Jayaprakash Narayan
x: The Swadeshi Movement (1905), not the JP Movement, was the first student-led national movement. Derozio founded the Young Bengal movement, India's first youth reform movement, and Jayaprakash Narayan led the 1974 Bihar student movement.

s: Which Chief Minister of Gujarat resigned in February 1974 following the Nav Nirman movement?
x: The Nav Nirman student movement against corruption and prices forced Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel to resign in February 1974.

s: Which was the first nationwide student mobilisation in India after Independence?
x: The JP movement of 1974, which began in Bihar, was the first nationwide post-Independence student mobilisation.

s: In which year did the AASU-led Assam Movement against illegal migrants begin?
x: The AASU movement ran from 1979 to 1985 and ended with the Assam Accord of 1985.

s: Which movement of 2011 is regarded as the first major anti-corruption youth movement in India?
x: India Against Corruption (2011) was the first major anti-corruption youth movement.

s: With which university were the Telangana student movements of 1969 and 2009-14 chiefly associated?
x: Osmania University students led the Telangana agitations of 1969 and 2009-14 for separate statehood.

s: The Jai Andhra agitation (1972–73) followed the Supreme Court's decision upholding which of the following?
x: The Jai Andhra agitation arose after the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and ended with the Six-Point Formula in 1973.

s: In which year did the 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' agitation for a steel plant at Visakhapatnam take place?
x: The agitation took place in 1966, with T. Amrutha Rao undertaking a fast.

s: With whose fast is the 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' agitation associated?
x: The 1966 agitation for a steel plant at Visakhapatnam saw T. Amrutha Rao's fast and deaths in police firing.

s: Which of the following ended the Jai Andhra agitation (1972-73)?
x: Jai Andhra was ended by the Six-Point Formula of 1973.

s: How is the new pattern of youth protest, as in Bangladesh 2024, usually organised?
o: Under a formally constituted central committee
Through youth wings of political parties
x: The new pattern is leaderless, digital protest organised on encrypted apps, with no formal central committee.

s: Which of the following pairs of youth unrest forms and examples is correctly matched?
x: The Dalit Panthers (1972, Maharashtra) are an example of militancy; secessionist movements include Naga, Assam and Khalistan.

s: Among the forms of youth unrest, under which is drug abuse classed?
x: Drug abuse is listed as deviance among the forms of youth unrest.

s: When and where did the Dalit Panthers emerge as a militant movement?
x: The Dalit Panthers emerged in 1972 in Maharashtra and are associated with militancy.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of youth unrest?
o: Identity crisis among youth is a cause of youth unrest.
The generation gap is growing as families become nuclear.
Families in India are increasingly becoming nuclear.
The generation gap is shrinking as families become nuclear.
x: The identity crisis and generation gap grow, not shrink, as Indian families become nuclear.

s: About how many people join India's working-age group each year (2021-31)?
x: About 9.7 million join the working-age group each year, which feeds jobless-growth unrest.

s: According to MoSPI 2022, what was the youth unemployment rate?
x: For youth aged 15–29 years, the reported unemployment rates were 13.0% for males and 12.5% for females.

s: Which of the following correctly states the youth unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is reported as 17.5%, higher than the national rate.

s: As per Census 2011, youth (15-24 years) formed about what share of India's population?
x: Census 2011 counted about 231 million youth (15-24), around 19.1% of the population.

s: As per Census 2011, what was the youth (15-24 years) population of India?
x: Census 2011 put youth (15-24) at about 231 million.

s: As per the PLFS 2025 annual report, what was India's youth (15-29) unemployment rate?
x: PLFS 2025 put youth unemployment at 9.9%, down from 10.3%; urban 13.6%, rural 8.3%.

s: In Andhra Pradesh (PLFS 2023-24), among which group was the youth unemployment rate highest?
x: AP's urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%, against an overall 17.5%.

s: As per the ILO (2026), what is the global youth unemployment rate?
x: The ILO puts global youth unemployment at 12.4% (67 million); 9.9% is India's PLFS 2025 figure.

s: As per Census 2011, about how many adolescents (10-19 years) were there in India?
x: Census 2011 counted about 253 million adolescents (10-19), about 20.9% of the population; 231 million is the youth (15-24) figure.

s: Which of the following pairs of Durkheim's suicide types and causes is NOT correctly matched?
x: Fatalistic suicide is associated with too much regulation; too little regulation marks anomic suicide.

s:
Consider the following statements about NCRB's ADSI 2024 report:
1. It recorded 1,70,746 suicides.
2. Daily wagers formed about 31% of the suicides.
3. Drug-overdose deaths fell by about 50%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ADSI 2024 recorded 1,70,746 suicides, about 31% of them daily wagers. Statement 3 is wrong: drug-overdose deaths (978) rose by 50%, not fell. So '1 and 2 only'.

s: According to Durkheim, what does anomic suicide result from?
x: Anomic suicide arises from too little regulation; fatalistic suicide from too much regulation.

s: In which year was Durkheim's study 'Le Suicide' published?
x: Durkheim's Le Suicide appeared in 1897.

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which was the leading cause of farmer suicides in India?
x: ADSI 2015 ranked bankruptcy or indebtedness first among causes of farmer suicides, followed by farming-related issues.

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which cause ranked second among causes of farmer suicides?
x: Farming-related issues came second after bankruptcy or indebtedness in ADSI 2015.

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2024, which State recorded the highest number of suicides?
x: Maharashtra recorded the most suicides in 2024 (22,174), followed by Tamil Nadu (19,965) and Madhya Pradesh.

s: In which year was the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, the main law in India on sex trafficking, enacted?
x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 is the main law on sex trafficking.

s: As per NCRB's Crime in India 2020, how many Anti Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) existed across States/UTs?
x: NCRB reported 696 AHTUs across States/UTs; MHA has funded AHTUs covering all districts.

s: Which case held Section 309 IPC, punishing attempted suicide, invalid in 1994?
x: P. Rathinam (1994) held Section 309 invalid; Section 309 made attempted suicide punishable with imprisonment up to one year and/or fine.

s: Tele-MANAS is a tele-mental-health helpline launched on 10 October 2022. What is its toll-free number?
x: Tele-MANAS was launched on 10 October 2022 and can be accessed through the toll-free number 14416.

s: Which section of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 presumes severe stress in a person who attempts suicide?
x: Section 115 of the MHCA 2017 presumes severe stress, so there is no trial or punishment and the State must provide care.

s:
Consider the following statements about attempted suicide in law:
1. The Law Commission's 210th Report recommended deleting Section 309 IPC.
2. Section 309 IPC provided imprisonment of up to three months.
3. Section 226 of BNS 2023 deals with an attempt to coerce a public servant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Section 309 provided simple imprisonment up to one year, not three months.

s: Which city was declared the first beggar-free city in 2025?
x: Indore was declared the first beggar-free city in 2025.

s: SMILE, launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 2022, includes a sub-scheme for which of the following?
o: Construction of prisons for habitual beggars
Removal of beggars from all urban areas
Comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging
x: SMILE includes a sub-scheme for comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging and shifts towards rights-based rehabilitation.

s: In which year did the Delhi High Court decriminalise begging in Delhi in the case associated with Harsh Mander?
x: The Delhi High Court decriminalised begging in 2018; in 2021 the Supreme Court refused to ban begging, calling it a socio-economic problem.

s: Which punitive anti-begging law has been copied by many States?
x: The Bombay Prevention of Begging Act, 1959 is the punitive model many States copied.

s: Which State tops the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's state-wise list of beggars?
x: West Bengal has the highest number of beggars in the Ministry of Social Justice list.

s: What did the Supreme Court decide in 2021 on a plea to ban begging?
o: It refused to ban begging, calling it a socio-economic problem
It banned begging in all public places
It upheld the punishment of beggars under the Bombay Act
It directed all States to arrest habitual beggars
x: In 2021 the Supreme Court refused to ban begging, saying it is a socio-economic problem.

s: Who led the Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Dubagunta Rosamma led the Anti-Arrack Movement among neo-literate women of the literacy campaign.

s: The Anti-Arrack Movement of 1992 began in Dubagunta village of which district?
x: The movement began in 1992 in Dubagunta village of Nellore district, led by Dubagunta Rosamma.

s: Article 47 directs the State to endeavour to prohibit, except for medicinal purposes, the consumption of which of the following?
o: Intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health
x: Article 47, a Directive Principle, refers to prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Anti-Arrack Movement:
1. It was led by neo-literate women of the literacy campaign.
2. It began in Nizamabad district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. The movement began in 1992 in Dubagunta village of Nellore district, not Nizamabad.

s: Who founded the Social Purity Association (1891), a temperance campaign?
x: R. Venkataratnam Naidu's Social Purity Association (1891) was a temperance campaign, a precedent for anti-liquor activism.

s: India lies between which two major drug-producing regions?
x: India lies between the Golden Crescent and the Golden Triangle, two major drug-producing regions.

s: According to the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use (2019), the most-used substance in India was:
x: Alcohol (14.6%) was the most-used substance, followed by cannabis (2.8%) and opioids (2.1%).

s: Which body implements the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan?
x: NMBA, launched by MoSJE on 15 August 2020, is implemented by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD).

s: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was initially launched in how many districts?
x: NMBA (MoSJE, 15 Aug 2020) began in 272 districts and now covers all.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – Ministry of Home Affairs
x: Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat is run by MoYAS via MY Bharat; NMBA belongs to MoSJE.

s: According to the 2019 National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use, which was the second most-used substance in India?
x: Alcohol (14.6%) came first, cannabis (2.8%) second and opioids (2.1%) third.

s: In which year was the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
x: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 15 August 2020 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Which institution conducted the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use (2019) with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
x: The 2019 survey was done by MoSJE with AIIMS-NDDTC; it found alcohol the most-used substance.

s: With which campaign is the Kashi Declaration (July 2025) associated?
o: Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat
x: The Kashi Declaration (July 2025) is part of the MoYAS campaign Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat, run through MY Bharat.

s: Under which Ministry does the National Institute of Social Defence function?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
x: NISD works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Which of the following describes the changing approach towards social problems such as suicide, drug abuse and beggary?
o: From statutory regulation towards complete absence of regulation
From health and rehabilitation towards punishment alone
From punishment towards health and rehabilitation
x: The approach is moving from punishment, including Section 309 and anti-begging laws, towards health and rehabilitation through measures such as MHCA, SMILE and NMBA.

s: Under GO 43 of Andhra Pradesh, how much ex gratia is paid to the family of a farmer who dies by suicide?
x: AP pays Rs 7 lakh ex gratia to farmer-suicide families under GO 43.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's liquor policy 2024:
1. Retail liquor sale was shifted to private licensees selected by lottery.
2. A 180 ml quarter was priced at Rs 99.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: retail moved to private licensees by lottery, with a Rs 99 price for a 180 ml quarter.

s: 'Dharya Sparsa – Operation Flush-Out' against drugs and illegal liquor was launched by the police of which AP district?
x: Chittoor Police launched 'Dharya Sparsa – Operation Flush-Out' in July 2026.

s: By whom, where and when was the term 'social exclusion' coined?
x: The term was coined by René Lenoir in France in 1974.

s: On what view does the Union mainly oppose a creamy layer for SCs and STs?
o: Caste exclusion exists only in urban areas
Income alone does not end caste-based exclusion
Economic criteria cannot be used in any welfare policy
x: The stated position is that income does not eliminate caste exclusion, so economic advancement alone does not end caste-based discrimination.

s: What is the process that shuts people out of facilities, benefits and opportunities that others enjoy called?
x: This is the standard definition of social exclusion, whose bases include caste, gender, disability, religion and region.

s: Which of the following is NOT a practice leading to social exclusion?
o: Denied access to land and water
x: Untouchability, segregation and denied access to land, water and jobs lead to exclusion; MGNREGA wage employment is a policy response to it.

s: Denial of property, work and mobility to women is an example of social exclusion based on which of the following?
x: Denying women property, work and mobility is exclusion on the basis of gender.

s: To how many days does the VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025 raise the rural employment guarantee?
x: The VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025, passed on 18 December 2025, proposed raising the guarantee from 100 to 125 days and changing the funding pattern.

s: On which date was NREGA renamed the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA (MGNREGA)?
x: NREGA was enacted in 2005, came into force on 2 February 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the original MGNREGA guarantee?
o: A legal right to 100 days of unskilled wage work per rural household per year
Payment of unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days
Social audits by the Gram Sabha
Reservation of exactly half of all workdays for women
x: The guarantee required that one-third of workers be women, not exactly half. The 100-day legal guarantee, 15-day unemployment allowance and Gram Sabha social audits are features of MGNREGA.

s: Under MGNREGA, at least what share of the workers must be women?
x: At least one-third of MGNREGA workers must be women, not half.

s: Under MGNREGA, if work is not provided within how many days of demand is an unemployment allowance due?
x: If work is not given within 15 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is payable.

s: NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, starting in which district?
x: NREGA first came into force on 2 February 2006 starting from Anantapur district in Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. Social audits are held by the Gram Sabha.
2. The right to work it guarantees is a Fundamental Right in Part III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gram Sabhas hold social audits; MGNREGA follows the Directive Principles, and the right to work is not in Part III.

s: To whom is the MGNREGA guarantee of at least 100 days of wage work in a financial year given?
o: Each adult individual in rural areas
x: The 100-day guarantee is per rural household in a financial year, not per adult individual.

s: In which year was the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act passed by Parliament?
x: NREGA was passed in August 2005; it came into force on 2 February 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

s: In which year was the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) introduced?
x: SGSY came in 1999, after IRDP (1978–80) and before NREGA (2005–06) and DAY-NRLM (2011).

s: Which was the first state-level employment guarantee scheme in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh Rural Employment Scheme of 1978
x: The Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme, introduced in 1972, was the first state scheme of this kind.

s: DAY-NRLM (2011) was a restructuring of which scheme?
x: DAY-NRLM restructured SGSY, an SHG-based self-employment scheme, not JRY, which was a wage-employment scheme.

s: PMEGP (2008) was formed by merging which schemes?
x: PMEGP merged PMRY and REGP and gives a credit-linked subsidy through KVIC; JRY merged NREP and RLEGP.

s: DWCRA (1982-83) was a sub-scheme of IRDP meant to reach which group?
x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of IRDP so that benefits reached rural women directly; TRYSEM trained rural youth.

s: Which programmes were merged to form the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana in 1989?
x: JRY (1989) merged the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) into one wage-employment scheme.

s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their launch:
1. SGSY
2. IRDP
3. JRY
4. DAY-NRLM
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: IRDP came in 1978-80, JRY in 1989, SGSY in 1999 and DAY-NRLM in 2011.

s: What was the main aim of TRYSEM, launched in 1979 as a component of IRDP?
x: TRYSEM (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment) trained rural youth and was a part of IRDP.

s: Which programmes were merged to form the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) in 1999?
x: SGSY (1999) merged IRDP, DWCRA, TRYSEM and others into one SHG-based self-employment scheme.

s: Through which body is the credit-linked subsidy under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP, 2008) given?
x: PMEGP merged PMRY and REGP and gives a credit-linked subsidy through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

s: Who propounded the concept of the “culture of poverty” in 1959?
x: The concept of the “culture of poverty” was propounded by Oscar Lewis in 1959.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the social indicators of poverty?
x: Illiteracy, malnutrition, poor health care and lack of safe water and sanitation are social indicators of poverty; size of the house is not one.

s: What is being poor compared with others in the same society called?
x: Relative poverty means being poor in comparison with others in the same society; absolute poverty is spending below a fixed poverty line.

s: On which of the following is India's official poverty line based?
x: India's official poverty line is consumption-based, set by Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE), not income.

s: Which is the nodal agency for poverty estimation, using NSSO data?
x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for poverty estimation; it replaced the Planning Commission and uses NSSO data.

s: Under the Current Daily Status, for what period is activity recorded?
o: Only the day of the survey
Each day of the reference week
x: Current Daily Status records activity for each day of the reference week, not only the day of the survey.

s: Which survey is the standard for unemployment data in India?
x: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) of the NSO is the standard for unemployment data (APPSC Group 2, 2025 key).

s: What reference period does the Current Weekly Status under PLFS use?
x: Current Weekly Status covers the 7 days before the survey; usual status covers the reference year.

s: At what interval is the NSO's Household Consumption Expenditure Survey conducted?
x: The HCES is conducted about every 5 years, and its MPCE data set the poverty line.

s: Under PLFS, which status measures a person's activity over the reference year?
x: Usual status looks at activity over the reference year; CWS uses 7 days and CDS each day of the week.

s: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index has three equally weighted dimensions and how many indicators?
x: The National MPI, prepared by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, has 3 dimensions and 12 indicators.

s: According to the NITI Multidimensional Poverty Index for 2023, which State recorded the highest poverty level?
x: Bihar recorded the highest multidimensional poverty level in the NITI MPI 2023, at 33.76%.

s: With which bodies does NITI Aayog build the National Multidimensional Poverty Index?
x: The National MPI is built by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.

s: As per NITI MPI 2023, what was the multidimensional poverty headcount of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's headcount was 6.06% (rank 9th), well below India's 14.96%; Bihar recorded 33.76%.

s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension of the National MPI?
x: Cooking fuel, bank accounts and electricity are standard-of-living indicators; nutrition belongs to the health dimension.

s: In the NITI Aayog National MPI 2023, what was Andhra Pradesh's rank with a poverty headcount of 6.06%?
x: Andhra Pradesh had an MPI headcount of 6.06% and was ranked 9th (NITI MPI 2023).

s: As per the NITI Aayog National MPI 2023 (2019-21 data), what was India's multidimensional poverty headcount?
x: India's headcount was 14.96%; Andhra Pradesh 6.06%; Bihar the highest at 33.76%.

s: As per NITI MPI 2023, which State had the lowest multidimensional poverty?
x: Kerala recorded the lowest MPI poverty and Bihar (33.76%) the highest.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what was the unemployment rate of Andhra Pradesh?
x: PLFS 2023–24 shows 4.1 per cent unemployment for Andhra Pradesh against 3.2 per cent for India.

s: In which sector is disguised unemployment, where extra workers add near-zero output, mainly found?
x: Disguised unemployment means more workers than needed, with near-zero marginal productivity, mainly on family farms in agriculture.

s: Which type of unemployment is caused by a mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available?
x: Structural unemployment is a long-term mismatch between skills and available jobs.

s: Which type of unemployment arises from a fall in labour demand during an economic slowdown?
x: Cyclical unemployment follows the trade cycle, rising when labour demand falls in a slowdown.

s: Which of the following pairs (unemployment type – predominant area) is correctly matched?
x: Educated and frictional unemployment are urban; disguised and seasonal unemployment are mainly in agriculture.

s: Which type of unemployment is temporary and occurs while workers are changing or searching for jobs?
x: Frictional unemployment is short-term joblessness while people change or look for jobs; it is mainly urban.

s: In which sector is seasonal unemployment mainly found in India?
x: Seasonal unemployment means work only in some months of the year; it is mainly found in agriculture.

s: As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey, what was India's unemployment rate in 2023-24?
x: PLFS shows India's unemployment rate fell from 6.0% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24).

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what was the labour force participation rate (LFPR) of Andhra Pradesh?
x: PLFS 2023-24 put Andhra Pradesh's LFPR at 47.5%.

s: Who chaired the Rangarajan Committee, which dealt with poverty measurement?
x: C. Rangarajan chaired the Rangarajan Expert Group (set up 2012, report 2014). Suresh Tendulkar chaired the earlier 2005 group, while S.R. Hashim (urban BPL households) and N.C. Saxena (rural BPL census) headed the 2009 groups.

s: On what calorie requirements was the Y.K. Alagh Committee's poverty estimation method based?
o: 2,700 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,400 calories in rural areas and 2,100 calories in urban areas
2,100 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,200 calories in both rural and urban areas
x: The Y.K. Alagh Committee, formed in 1979, used a calorie norm of 2,400 calories for rural areas and 2,100 calories for urban areas. The corresponding expenditure was treated as the poverty line.

s: Which of the following was a significant departure introduced by the Tendulkar Committee methodology?
o: It used only rural consumption baskets for both sectors.
It excluded non-food expenditure from the poverty line.
It restored the calorie anchor as the sole basis of poverty estimation.
It dropped the calorie anchor and included health and education expenditure.
x: The Tendulkar Committee (report 2009) dropped the calorie anchor, used the Mixed Reference Period (MRP), applied the urban basket to both sectors and included health and education spending. The other options are wrong: it did not use a rural-only basket, exclude non-food spending or restore the calorie anchor.

s: What were the Rangarajan poverty lines for 2011-12?
o: ₹32 per day rural and ₹47 per day urban
₹32 per day urban and ₹47 per day rural
₹47 per day in both rural and urban areas
₹27 per day rural and ₹33 per day urban
x: Rangarajan estimated ₹32 per day for rural and ₹47 per day for urban areas (₹972 and ₹1,407 per month).

s: Which poverty estimation method used CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas?
x: The Lakdawala methodology kept the calorie base, used state-specific poverty lines and applied CPI-AL for rural and CPI-IW for urban areas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.R. Hashim Expert Group – Rural BPL census
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Rural BPL census methodology
Rangarajan Committee – Chaired by Bimal Jalan
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Urban BPL households
x: N.C. Saxena dealt with the rural BPL census and S.R. Hashim with urban BPL identification; C. Rangarajan chaired the Rangarajan Committee.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was poverty in 2023-24 as measured by the Tendulkar line?
x: Poverty measured by the Tendulkar line was stated to have fallen from 21.9 percent in 2011–12 to 2.3 percent in 2023–24.

s: In which year was the Y.K. Alagh Task Force on poverty estimation set up?
x: The Alagh Task Force (1979) used a calorie-only norm of 2,400 rural and 2,100 urban.

s: According to the Tendulkar methodology, what was poverty in India in 2011-12?
x: The Tendulkar line put poverty at 21.9% in 2011-12; 37.2% was its 2004-05 figure and 2.3% the 2023-24 figure.

s: In October 2025, which body updated the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022-23?
x: In October 2025 the RBI updated the Rangarajan line using HCES 2022-23 and a poverty-line-basket price index.

s: Which expert group included both food and non-food needs such as housing, clothing, education, health and transport in its poverty line?
x: The Rangarajan Expert Group (report 2014) built its poverty line on separate food and non-food needs.

s: In which year was the Tendulkar Expert Group on poverty estimation set up?
x: The Tendulkar Expert Group was set up in 2005 and gave its report in 2009.

s: According to the Tendulkar Expert Group, what was the poverty ratio in India in 2004-05?
x: The Tendulkar method put poverty at 37.2% in 2004-05 and 21.9% in 2011-12.

s: Which expert group's method gave a poverty estimate of 27.5% for 2004-05?
x: The Lakdawala method (state-specific lines with CPI-AL / CPI-IW) gave 27.5% poverty for 2004-05.

s: What were the monthly per capita poverty lines for 2011-12 set by the Rangarajan Expert Group for rural and urban areas respectively?
x: Rangarajan's lines were ₹972 (rural) and ₹1,407 (urban) a month, i.e. about ₹32 and ₹47 a day.

s: Which expert group was set up in 2009 to recommend the method of identifying urban BPL households?
x: The S.R. Hashim group (2009) dealt with urban BPL households; N.C. Saxena dealt with the rural BPL census.

s: Which expert group on poverty adopted the Mixed Reference Period (MRP) and used the urban consumption basket for both rural and urban areas?
x: The Tendulkar group (report 2009) adopted MRP, used the urban basket for both sectors and dropped the calorie anchor.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Tendulkar Expert Group:
1. It adopted the Mixed Reference Period (MRP).
2. It fixed calorie norms of 2,400 for rural and 2,100 for urban areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tendulkar adopted MRP and dropped the calorie anchor; the 2,400 / 2,100 calorie norms were the Alagh Task Force's (1979).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about poverty by social group in India?
o: Scheduled Tribes have the highest incidence of poverty.
Discrimination contributes to poverty among these groups.
Scheduled Tribes rank below Scheduled Castes in poverty incidence.
Social exclusion is a cause of poverty among these groups.
x: Scheduled Tribes have the highest poverty incidence, with Scheduled Castes next, so STs do not rank below SCs.

s: Which social group has the highest incidence of poverty in India?
x: Scheduled Tribes have the highest poverty, followed by Scheduled Castes (ST > SC > others).

s: As per 2025-26 data, what was the share of informal employment in rural Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rural informal employment in AP was 62.3%; 47.5% is AP's LFPR and 64.3% is social protection coverage.

s: India's social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to what in 2025?
x: Social protection coverage rose from 22% (2016) to 64.3% (2025).

s: Gig workers form roughly what share of India's workforce (2025-26)?
x: Gig workers make up 2%+ of the workforce; migrant, casual and unorganised workers have little social security.

s: In India, what kind of right is the right to vote?
o: Statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act
x: The right to vote is only a statutory right, conferred by Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act. It is not a Fundamental Right (Art. 19 lists freedoms of speech, movement etc.), a Directive Principle (Art. 47 concerns nutrition, health and prohibition) or a Fundamental Duty. This shows that not every human right is a Fundamental Right.

s: Which 1993 document affirmed the indivisibility and interdependence of human rights?
x: The Vienna Declaration of 1993 affirmed that civil-political and socio-economic rights are indivisible and interdependent.

s: In which year was the Magna Carta issued?
x: The Magna Carta dates to 1215, before the event of 1688, the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the French Revolution (1789).

s: Which of the following describes the nature of human rights?
o: Granted by the State to citizens
Inherent and inalienable to every human being
Available only to citizens of UN members
x: Human rights are inherent and inalienable rights held simply because one is human, resting on human dignity.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every Fundamental Right is a human right.
2. Every human right is a Fundamental Right in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Every Fundamental Right is a human right, but not every human right (for example, the right to vote, which is statutory) is a Fundamental Right.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about human rights and Fundamental Rights in India?
o: Every Fundamental Right is a human right
Not every human right is a Fundamental Right
The right to vote is a statutory right
The right to vote is a Fundamental Right under Part III
x: The right to vote in India is only a statutory right, not a Fundamental Right; Fundamental Rights are a part of the wider body of human rights.

s: Which value lies at the core of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
x: The UDHR was drafted after the atrocities of the Second World War to protect human dignity, which is at its core.

s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights covers which rights?
o: Civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights
Only economic, social and cultural rights
x: The UDHR covers all five categories of rights, though it is not a treaty and is not legally binding as one.

s: The right to privacy is protected under which articles of the UDHR and the ICCPR respectively?
x: The UDHR protects privacy under Article 12 and the ICCPR under Article 17.

s: Which of the following is identified as an economic and social right under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
x: The right to work is an economic and social right in the UDHR. Free speech, freedom of religion and equality before law are civil and political rights.

s: Who chaired the committee that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
x: Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the UDHR drafting; Karel Vasak proposed the generations and Peter Benenson founded Amnesty.

s: In which year was Human Rights Day on 10 December set by UNGA resolution 423(V)?
x: UNGA resolution 423(V) of 1950 fixed 10 December as Human Rights Day.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UDHR:
1. It was adopted on 10 December 1948.
2. It has a Preamble and 30 articles.
3. It is a legally binding treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948 with a Preamble and 30 articles, but it is not a treaty and not legally binding.

s: What was the theme of Human Rights Day observed in December 2024?
o: Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now
Dignity, Freedom and Justice for All
Stand up for someone's rights today
Equality: Reducing inequalities, advancing human rights
x: Human Rights Day on 10 December 2024 had the theme 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.

s: What was the theme of Human Rights Day observed on 10 December 2025?
o: Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now
Stand up for someone's rights today
Dignity, Freedom and Justice for All
x: The UN theme for Human Rights Day 2025 was 'Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials'; 2024's was 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.

s: In which year was 'Stand up for someone's rights today' the theme of Human Rights Day?
x: 'Stand up for someone's rights today' was the slogan of Human Rights Day 2016, launched by the UN Human Rights Office.

s: Which of the following statements about the Universal Declaration of Human Rights is incorrect?
o: It was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948.
It was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1950.
It contains a Preamble and 30 Articles.
It was prepared after the atrocities of World War II to safeguard human dignity.
x: Option B is incorrect: the UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948, not 1950. It has a Preamble and 30 Articles and was drafted after the Second World War.

s: Where was Amnesty International founded in 1961?
x: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977; the New York-based body is Human Rights Watch.

s: Where is Human Rights Watch based?
x: Human Rights Watch is New York-based; Amnesty International was founded in London.

s: Since which year has the UN Human Rights Prize, given usually every five years, been awarded?
x: The UNGA has given the UN Human Rights Prize since 1968, usually every five years.

s: Who founded Amnesty International in 1961?
x: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson; it won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

s: In which year did Amnesty International receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: Amnesty International won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977; it was founded in 1961.

s: Which of the following is a third-generation (collective) human right?
x: Third-generation rights are collective: healthy environment, development and peace; work is second-generation, speech and fair trial first.

s: When did the UN General Assembly recognise the Right to Water and Sanitation?
x: The Right to Water and Sanitation was recognised on 28 July 2010; the Right to Development came in 1986 and the environment right on 28 July 2022.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Declaration on the Right to Development?
x: The right to development was recognised by a UNGA Declaration in 1986.

s: How many seats does the Eastern European group hold in the UN Human Rights Council?
x: Eastern Europe has 6 seats; Africa and Asia-Pacific have 13 each and Latin America and the Caribbean 8.

s: Which body did the UN Human Rights Council, formed in 2006, replace?
o: Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
x: The Human Rights Council was formed in 2006 as the successor to the UN Commission on Human Rights; it is based in Geneva.

s: A member of the UN Human Rights Council can serve at most how many consecutive terms?
x: Members are elected by the UNGA for three-year terms and may serve at most two consecutive terms.

s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Universal Periodic Review (UPR)?
o: It examines only the implementation of economic and social rights.
It is a peer review of the human rights record of every UN member state.
It is a judicial review conducted only for states accused of treaty violations.
It is a review conducted by the International Court of Justice every three years.
x: The UPR is a peer review of the human rights record of every UN member state, conducted under the Human Rights Council.

s: Following which conference was the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights set up in 1993?
x: The OHCHR was established in 1993 after the Vienna Conference.

s: How many members does the UN Human Rights Council have?
x: The Human Rights Council has 47 members elected by the UNGA for three-year terms.

s: How many seats does the Asia-Pacific group hold in the UN Human Rights Council?
x: Asia-Pacific and Africa hold 13 seats each; Latin America 8, Western Europe and Others 7, Eastern Europe 6.

s: By what UNGA vote can a UN Human Rights Council member be suspended for gross violations?
x: A two-thirds vote of the UNGA can suspend a member for gross violations.

s: Who are the special rapporteurs under the Human Rights Council's special procedures?
o: Paid UN staff of the OHCHR
Judges of the International Court of Justice
x: Special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts on a theme or country under the HRC special procedures.

s: In which year did the Universal Periodic Review, held in cycles of about 4.5 years, begin?
x: The UPR, a peer review of every UN member's record, has run since 2008 in cycles of about 4.5 years.

s: Where is the UN Human Rights Council based?
x: The Human Rights Council, set up in 2006, is based in Geneva.

s: What is the term of a member of the UN Human Rights Council?
x: Members of the 47-member Council are elected by the UNGA for 3-year terms, at most two in a row.

s:
Match the following regional groups with their seats in the UN Human Rights Council:
List-I
A. Africa
B. Latin America and Caribbean
C. Western Europe and Others
D. Eastern Europe
List-II
1. 6
2. 7
3. 8
4. 13
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Of the 47 seats, Africa has 13, Latin America and Caribbean 8, Western Europe and Others 7 and Eastern Europe 6.

s: In which year were the Paris Principles relating to national human rights institutions adopted by the UN General Assembly?
x: The Paris Principles were adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Paris Principles?
o: Exclusive dependence on the executive for investigations
A broad mandate set out in law
x: The Paris Principles require independence and autonomy from government and powers to investigate; exclusive dependence on the executive is contrary to these requirements.

s: Which of the following pairs about GANHRI accreditation is correctly matched?
o: 'A' status – Partly compliant with the Paris Principles
'B' status – Fully compliant with the Paris Principles
Sub-Committee on Accreditation – Accredits NHRIs for GANHRI
'A' status – Non-compliant with the Paris Principles
x: GANHRI accredits NHRIs through its Sub-Committee on Accreditation; 'A' means fully and 'B' partly compliant.

s: When were the Paris Principles, in conformity with which the NHRC was constituted, adopted in Paris?
x: The Paris Principles were adopted in Paris in October 1991. They were endorsed by the UN General Assembly on 20 December 1993.

s: Which of the following does GANHRI accredit?
x: GANHRI accredits national human-rights institutions through its Sub-Committee on Accreditation: 'A' means fully and 'B' partly compliant with the Paris Principles.

s: Who proposed the three-generation classification of human rights in 1977?
x: Karel Vasak proposed the three generations in 1977, mapped to liberty, equality and fraternity.

s: In Karel Vasak's classification, the eradication of social discrimination falls under which generation of rights?
x: Eradication of social discrimination is grouped with work, education and health as a second-generation (equality) right.

s: In Karel Vasak's classification, with which ideal are third-generation human rights linked?
x: First, second and third generations correspond to liberty, equality and fraternity (solidarity).

s: Under the UDHR, how is the right to social security classed?
x: Work, education, social security and health are economic and social rights in the UDHR.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the ICCPR?
x: Article 19 of the ICCPR concerns expression. Privacy is protected under Article 17; the other three pairings are correct.

s: In which year was CEDAW adopted?
x: CEDAW came in 1979, after the UDHR (1948) and ICCPR (1966).

s: What does the International Bill of Human Rights comprise?
o: The ICCPR, ICESCR and the Vienna Declaration only
Only the UDHR and the ICCPR
The UDHR, UN Charter and International Court of Justice Statute
The UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR and the optional protocols
x: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.

s: In which year was the Optional Protocol to the ICESCR adopted?
x: The ICESCR Optional Protocol was adopted in 2008; 1976 is when the two Covenants entered into force.

s: What is India's position on the ICCPR and its First Optional Protocol?
o: Not a party to the ICCPR at all
Party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed the First Optional Protocol
Party to the ICCPR since 1979 and signatory to the First Optional Protocol
Party only to the Second Optional Protocol, not the ICCPR
x: India has been a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed its First Optional Protocol, so its individual complaints procedure is unavailable.

s: Freedom of expression is protected under which Article of the ICCPR?
x: ICCPR Article 19 covers expression; Article 17 covers privacy, Article 14 fair trial and Article 24 child rights.

s: When did the ICESCR enter into force?
x: The ICESCR came into force on 3 January 1976, before the ICCPR (23 March 1976); both were adopted on 16 December 1966.

s: Since which year has India been a party to the ICCPR?
x: India is a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed its First Optional Protocol.

s: Which of the following entered into force first?
x: The ICESCR came into force on 3 January 1976, before the ICCPR (23 March 1976); CEDAW and CRC came later.

s: When did the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) enter into force?
x: The ICCPR, adopted on 16 December 1966, entered into force on 23 March 1976, after the ICESCR (3 January 1976).

s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is associated with which treaty and what change in the number of recognised disabilities?
x: The CRPD concerns persons with disabilities and gave rise to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.

s: What does the UN convention known as CPED deal with?
x: CPED concerns enforced disappearance; CMW covers migrant workers, CRPD persons with disabilities and CAT torture.

s: Which core UN human rights treaty has India not signed?
x: India has not signed the CMW; it ratified CRPD in 2007 and signed CPED in 2007 without ratifying it.

s: What is India's status with respect to the Convention against Torture (CAT)?
x: India signed CAT in 1997 but has not ratified it; CAT and CPED are signed but not ratified, and CMW is not signed.

s: In which year did India ratify CEDAW?
x: India ratified CEDAW in 1993; CEDAW itself dates from 1979.

s: Which convention did India accede to on 11 December 1992?
x: India acceded to the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) on 11 December 1992.

s: Which UN convention, ratified by India in 1968, deals with racial discrimination?
x: CERD (1965) deals with racial discrimination; India ratified it in 1968.

s: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution corresponds to which Article of the UDHR?
x: Article 21 corresponds to UDHR Article 3; Article 14 matches UDHR Article 7, Article 32 Article 8 and Article 23 Article 4.

s: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights is available to both citizens and foreigners?
o: Article 30 right of minorities to establish educational institutions
Article 29 protection of language and script of citizens
Article 21 protection of life and personal liberty
x: Articles 14, 20, 21, 23 and 25 to 28 are available to citizens and foreigners alike. Article 19 is available only to citizens.

s: Under which Article is bonded labour constitutionally prohibited?
x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, including bonded labour.

s: Under which Part of the Constitution does Article 40, on village panchayats, fall?
o: Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV)
x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV, while Articles 14 and 32 are Fundamental Rights in Part III.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 23 – Prohibition of employment of children in factories
Article 22 – Protection against arrest and detention
Article 20 – Protection in respect of conviction for offences
Article 24 – Prohibition of employment of children in factories
x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour; child employment in factories is Article 24.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Articles 29–30 – Cultural and educational rights of minorities
Article 21A – Cultural and educational rights of minorities
x: Article 21A is the Right to Education, inserted by the 86th Amendment; minorities' rights are in Articles 29–30.

s: Which Article of the Constitution defines the 'State' for the Fundamental Rights?
x: Article 12 defines 'State'; Article 15 prohibits discrimination and Article 18 abolishes titles.

s: Which Article of the Constitution makes laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void?
x: Article 13 makes laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void, which is the basis of judicial review.

s: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution corresponds to which Article of the UDHR?
x: Article 14 (equality before law) matches UDHR Article 7; Article 21 matches Article 3 and Article 32 matches Article 8.

s: Article 32 of the Constitution (constitutional remedies) parallels which UDHR Article?
x: Article 32, called the 'Heart and Soul' by Ambedkar, parallels UDHR Article 8.

s: Which Fundamental Right is available only to citizens?
x: Article 19's six freedoms are for citizens only; Articles 14, 20, 21, 23 and 25-28 also cover foreigners.

s: Abolition of Untouchability is provided under which Article?
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Article 14 is equality before law and Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Article 21A, the right to education for children aged 6 to 14?
x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making education for 6-14 year olds a Fundamental Right.

s: Who called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) the heart and soul of the Constitution.

s: Below what age does Article 24 prohibit the employment of children in factories, mines and hazardous work?
x: Article 24 bars employing children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

s: Which Articles together make up the Right against Exploitation?
x: The Right against Exploitation consists of Article 23 (traffic and forced labour) and Article 24 (child labour).

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 15(4), enabling special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs?
x: Article 15(4) was added by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the mechanisms under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
o: The NHRC functions at the State level.
The NHRC functions at the national level.
SHRCs function at the State level.
Human Rights Courts provide a district-level mechanism for speedy trials.
x: The NHRC is a national body; State-level work is done by the SHRCs.

s: What does the expression 'International Covenants' under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 refer to?
x: The Act defines International Covenants as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
x: The Ordinance was issued on 28 September 1993, while the NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993.

s: Under the PHRA, 1993, 'human rights' are rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity that are:
o: Recognised only as civil and political rights in the UDHR
Guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in International Covenants and enforceable by Indian courts
x: The statutory definition covers rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in International Covenants and enforceable by Indian courts.

s: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, which of the following is NOT included in the expression 'armed forces'?
o: Other armed forces of the Union
x: The Act defines armed forces as the naval, military and air forces and includes any other armed forces of the Union. State armed police are expressly not included, so complaints against them fall under the Commission's ordinary jurisdiction.

s: With whose concurrence does the State Government notify a Court of Session as a Human Rights Court?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Under Section 30, the State Government needs the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, not the Chief Justice of India.

s: For offences relating to what are proceedings of a Human Rights Commission deemed judicial proceedings?
o: Bribery and criminal breach of trust
False evidence and insulting a public servant in judicial proceedings
x: They are deemed judicial proceedings for false evidence (IPC 193) and insulting a public servant in judicial proceedings (IPC 228); corresponding BNS provisions apply from 1 July 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
1. Section 31 provides for a Special Public Prosecutor for every Human Rights Court.
2. The Special Public Prosecutor must be an advocate with at least seven years' practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Section 31 lets the State Government specify a Special Public Prosecutor, an advocate of at least 7 years' practice, for each Human Rights Court.

s: 'Public servant' under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 has the meaning in Section 21 of the IPC. Which BNS provision replaced it from 1 July 2024?
x: The IPC Section 21 definition of public servant is now Section 2(28) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

s: What are members and officers of the NHRC deemed to be?
x: The Act deems NHRC members and officers to be public servants.

s: What does 'armed forces' mean under Section 2(1)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act?
o: Only the Army, Navy and Air Force
Naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union
x: Section 2(1)(a) defines armed forces as the naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union.

s: To what do the arrest safeguards laid down in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal primarily relate?
o: Recognition of the right to livelihood
Protection of persons during arrest and custodial detention
x: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down safeguards intended to prevent custodial abuse and protect persons during arrest and detention.

s: In which case was the right to a speedy trial read into Article 21?
x: Hussainara Khatoon (1979) gave speedy trial; Hoskot legal aid, Olga Tellis livelihood, Francis Coralie dignity.

s: Which of the following pairs (right under Article 21 – case) is correctly matched?
x: Subhash Kumar (1991) gave a clean environment; privacy came from Puttaswamy (2017), livelihood from Olga Tellis, legal aid from Hoskot.

s: The right to privacy was held part of Article 21 in which case?
x: K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) recognised privacy under Article 21; D.K. Basu laid down arrest safeguards.

s: In which case was the right to livelihood read into Article 21?
x: In Olga Tellis (1985), the pavement dwellers case, the Supreme Court held that the right to life includes the right to livelihood.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to live with human dignity?
x: Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) read the right to live with human dignity into Article 21.

s: In which case was the right to free legal aid read into Article 21?
x: M.H. Hoskot (1978) read legal aid into Article 21; Hussainara Khatoon is speedy trial, Olga Tellis livelihood.

s:
Consider the following parts of the Indian Constitution:
1. Preamble
2. Directive Principles of State Policy
3. Fundamental Duties
In which of the above are the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights reflected?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: UDHR ideals of justice, equality and liberty are reflected in the Preamble, the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Duties.

s: Which Fundamental Duty is specifically related to protecting the dignity of women?
x: Article 51A(e) requires citizens to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

s: Which Article empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing international treaties and agreements?
x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for implementing treaties; Article 51(c) only directs respect for international law.

s: On which international instrument did the Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment rely substantially?
x: In Vishaka (1997), the Supreme Court relied on CEDAW to frame workplace-harassment guidelines.

s: In which 2003 case did PIL principles enable courts to rely on international conventions?
x: The principles of public interest litigation enabled courts to rely on international conventions in Guruvayur Devaswom (2003).

s: The NCPCR, set up in 2007, works in line with which international instrument?
x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 and works in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).

s: Which Directive Principle provides for maternity relief?
x: Article 42 provides humane conditions of work and maternity relief; Article 43 is the living wage.

s: Which Directive Principle provides for a living wage for workers?
x: Article 43 provides for a living wage; 39(a) covers livelihood, 39(d) equal pay and 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief.

s: Which Directive Principle asks the State to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations?
x: Article 51(c), a Directive Principle, asks the State to respect international law; Article 253 is Parliament's power to implement treaties.

s: Under the Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026, who issues the identity certificate?
x: The District Magistrate issues the certificate on a medical board's recommendation; self-perceived identity is excluded.

s: In which year was the National Green Tribunal Act enacted?
x: The National Green Tribunal Act dates from 2010, not 2013.

s: When did the Right to Information Act come into force?
x: The RTI Act got assent on 15 June 2005 and took effect on 12 October 2005, after 120 days.

s: Under the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, within what period must local bodies survey and build sanitary latrines?
x: Local bodies must do so within three years; the Act also bans cleaning sewers and septic tanks without protective gear.

s: In which year did the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 come into force?
x: The Domestic Violence Act was enacted in 2005 and came into force in 2006 (26 October 2006).

s: In which year was the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) enacted?
x: MISA, an internal security statute, was enacted in 1971.

s: Under the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, which is prohibited?
o: All sanitation work by local bodies
x: The 2013 Act bars sewer cleaning without protective gear and requires local bodies to survey and build sanitary latrines within 3 years.

s: When did the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 come into force?
x: The SC/ST Atrocities Act of 1989 came into force on 30 January 1990.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NHRC members — appointed by the Prime Minister
NHRC selection committee — headed by the Chief Minister
SHRC selection committee — headed by the Prime Minister
SHRC members — appointed by the Governor
x: The Governor appoints the SHRC; the President appoints the NHRC, the Prime Minister heads the NHRC selection panel and the Chief Minister the State one.

s: Under the PHRA, 1993, who appoints the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The NHRC is appointed by the President and the SHRC by the Governor; the selection committees are headed by the PM and CM.

s: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what is the status of constituting a State Human Rights Commission for a State Government?
o: Mandatory only through a constitutional amendment
x: The Act says a State Government 'may' constitute an SHRC, so it is optional.

s: By whom is the Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission constituted?
o: Parliament under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
The Andhra Pradesh Government under the PHRA, 1993
x: The AP SHRC is constituted by the Andhra Pradesh Government under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

s: To whom does the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission address the resignation?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Since 2006 the SHRC Chairperson resigns in writing to the Governor; the President only removes, and the Chief Minister heads the selection committee.

s: Who alone can remove the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The Governor appoints the SHRC Chairperson, but only the President can remove them.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the State Human Rights Commission after the 2006 amendment is correctly matched?
o: Strength of the SHRC – Three members including the Chairperson
Judicial member – A sitting Supreme Court Judge
Third member – A serving IAS officer
x: The 2006 amendment cut the SHRC from five to three: the Chairperson, a judicial member (HC or district judge) and a person with human-rights knowledge.

s: The annual report of a State Human Rights Commission is submitted to the State Government and thereafter laid before which body?
o: Parliament with a memorandum of action taken
State Legislature with a memorandum of action taken
x: The SHRC submits its annual report to the State Government, which lays it before the State Legislature along with a memorandum of action taken.

s:
Consider the following statements about a State Human Rights Commission:
1. In a vacancy in the office of Chairperson, the Governor may authorise a member to act as Chairperson.
2. The Chief Justice of the High Court is a member of the committee that selects its Chairperson.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Governor authorises an acting Chairperson; the High Court Chief Justice is only consulted for judge members and is not on the CM-led selection committee.

s: In a State having a Legislative Council, who are added to the committee that recommends the SHRC Chairperson and members?
o: Chairman and Leader of Opposition of the Legislative Council
Chief Justice of the High Court and Advocate General
Governor and Deputy Speaker of the Assembly
Chief Secretary and Director General of Police
x: The CM-led committee has the Speaker, State Home Minister and LoP in the Assembly; where there is a Council, its Chairman and LoP are added.

s: Which of the following pairs about the NHRC and SHRCs is correctly matched?
o: NHRC selection committee – Headed by the CJI
SHRC Chairperson – Removed by the Governor
SHRC selection committee – Headed by the Chief Minister
NHRC Chairperson – Resigns to the Vice-President
x: The SHRC selection committee is headed by the Chief Minister; the NHRC one by the PM. Both chairs are removed by the President, and the NHRC chair resigns to the President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC and SHRCs:
1. Both Chairpersons are removed by the President.
2. Both Chairpersons are appointed by the President.
3. The NHRC Chairperson resigns to the President and the SHRC Chairperson to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both chairs are removed by the President, but the SHRC chair is appointed by the Governor, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to State Human Rights Commissions is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Inquiry powers – Same civil-court powers as the NHRC
x: An SHRC has no power to punish violators or enforce its recommendations as decrees; they are advisory.

s: If a matter is already being inquired into by the NHRC, what will a State Human Rights Commission do?
o: Take it over with the Governor's approval
Inquire into it after one month
x: An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by the NHRC or another statutory commission.

s: Into violations relating to subjects in which List(s) does a State Human Rights Commission inquire?
x: An SHRC covers the State and Concurrent Lists; the NHRC covers all subjects.

s: After the 2019 change, which body handles the human-rights functions relating to Delhi?
o: An SHRC on which the Centre confers them
x: The Centre may confer a Union Territory's human-rights functions on an SHRC, but Delhi's are handled by the NHRC itself.

s: Which amendment reduced the members of a State Human Rights Commission from five to three?
x: The 2006 amendment cut SHRC members from five to three.
